subject: docs/coop/artifacts/section31-supplier-coverage.v2.json
protocol: D-000 independent review; refute not confirm; successor to v1 REJECT (S31-B1 from Claude 2; S31-CX-B1, S31-CX-B2 from Codex)
summary: All three named blockers landed and I verified each by executing the checker rather than by reading it. S31-B1 is repaired at the exact mutation that defeated v1: modifying a bound supplier's bytes while leaving path and selector intact now returns FAIL with DIGEST-MOVED at exit 1, where v1 returned PASS at exit 0. S31-CX-B1's ordering requirement is verified by construction and by execution -- the digest is computed at line 122 and fails at 124, before json.loads at 129, so a supplier corrupted to non-JSON reports DIGEST-MOVED rather than a parse error. S31-CX-B2's rebinding is exact: freeze item 3 asks for 'selected default custody/retention behavior, including whether any retention is implicit', and the new head carries durableDefault DURABLE_RETAINED and implicitDurableRetention YES, answering both limbs. Twelve mutation cases all fail closed. The blocker I record is on S31-1, the item neither reviewer examined in v1: it is marked BOUND while its head supplies three of the four claim categories freeze item 1 names, with no model for verdict claims. That is the same defect class as the repaired S31-CX-B2, differing in degree and not in kind, and it contradicts the discipline the artifact applies to itself at S31-2.

objections.claim: S31-1 is marked BOUND to a head that supplies three of the four claim categories its freeze item names. Freeze item 1 requires a model for verdict claims and the bound selector contains none.
evidence: Freeze item 1, verbatim from the artifact's own itemsVerbatim: 'exact evaluation-proof model for match, no-match, indeterminate/error, and verdict claims'. Four named categories.

The bound head is evaluation-proof.v8.json#$.proofObligationsByClaimShape. I read its full contents: a flat dict of six short strings keyed local-match, relationship-match, aggregate-match, no-match, indeterminate, error. Match is covered in three forms, no-match once, indeterminate and error once each. There is no verdict shape.
Token census inside the bound head: verdict 0, fate 0, outcome 0, decision 0. The head models proof obligations per claim shape and does not reach verdicts at all.

The word verdict occurs 38 times elsewhere in evaluation-proof.v8.json, across twelve other top-level keys -- canonicalCommitmentGrammar, normativePreimageGrammar, preimageGoldens, wireGrammars, persistedSchemaRegistry, invariants, positiveVectors, adversarialNegatives, policySemanticsV2, activationAuthority, semanticObjectBindingContract, identityStabilityFromEP7. None of them is the bound selector. The file may well supply the missing limb; the binding does not point at it.
counts.bound is 2 and the checker confirms bound=2, so the coverage total counts S31-1 as a fully bound item.
objections.whyItMatters: This is the defect Codex blocked v1 for, one item over. S31-CX-B2 was that S31-3's head 'does not contain those values'; here S31-1's head does not contain one of the four values its item names. The difference is partial rather than total coverage, which is a difference in degree, not in kind. It matters more than it would in an ordinary artifact because this instrument's entire product is a coverage count: a reader takes bound=2 to mean two of the eight mandatory items have a supplier that supplies them. The artifact also states the correct discipline itself, at S31-2's UNBOUND reason -- 'Binding a class document as if it were a recipe would pretend the recipes are settled.' S31-1 does the thing S31-2 refuses to do.
objections.remedy: Either extend or split the selector so the verdict-claims limb is actually supplied, or mark S31-1 with an explicit partial standing and state which limb is unsupplied. The artifact currently has only BOUND and UNBOUND; a partial state may need minting, which is itself a change worth naming.
objections.howIFoundIt: By applying to S31-1 the check I explicitly declined to run in my v1 review and that Codex ran on S31-3. See reviewerSelfCorrection.

objections.claim: The stated rationale justifies not pinning the head version but does not justify stopping at v8 rather than v9, which supersedes v8's proof obligations and carries the byte-identical selector content.
evidence: whyThisHead reads: 'Later evaluation-proof versions drop the six claim shapes. v8 remains the supplier of this item. Binding v8 is not applying v8 and is not a seal.'

The first sentence is TRUE, and I initially misjudged it -- see reviewerSelfCorrection. A full numeric sweep of all thirteen versions shows v1 through v9 carry six shapes and v10, v11, v12 and v13 have the key ABSENT.
But v9 is also a later version and does not drop them. I compared v8's and v9's proofObligationsByClaimShape directly: same six keys, and content equality is exact (a == b returns True).
evaluation-proof.v9.json declares supersedesProofObligationsOf: evaluation-proof.v8.json -- it claims succession over precisely the thing being bound.
There is no adopted-standing defence available: v8 and v9 are both status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL. Neither is applied; neither is sealed.
objections.whyItMatters: The instrument exists to keep supplier lineage visible, and theErrorThisExistsToPrevent is 'Conflating a successor still exists with the item's supplier selector still exists'. Here a successor exists AND still carries the selector with identical content, and the table pins the predecessor without saying why. Nothing substantive is lost, because the content is identical -- which is exactly why this is an advisory and not a blocker. But the one field whose job is to explain the choice of head explains a different choice than the one made.
objections.remedy: State the actual reason for stopping at v8 rather than v9, or re-pin to v9 and re-measure. If the reason is that v9 was not reviewed, say so.

objections.claim: The refusal list was not updated when S31-3 was rebound. It disclaims a file the table no longer binds and does not disclaim the file it now binds.
evidence: whatThisDoesNotDo[2] reads 'Does not apply evaluation-proof.v8 or retention-tiers.v28.'

v2's two bound suppliers are evaluation-proof.v8.json and product-dispositions.v1.json. retention-tiers.v28.json is not bound by any item in v2; it was S31-3's supplier in v1 and the S31-CX-B2 repair moved S31-3 to product-dispositions.v1.json#$.decisions.CD-RT-5.defaultPosture.
objections.whyItMatters: The refusal is load-bearing on this artifact: binding a supplier is not applying it, and the list is where that is said. The newly bound file is the one that most needs the disclaimer, because CD-RT-5 is a live product disposition that overrides a standing architectural recommendation. Saying 'does not apply' about a file no longer bound, while saying nothing about the file now bound, inverts the coverage of the refusal.
objections.remedy: Replace retention-tiers.v28 with product-dispositions.v1 in that refusal, or list all currently bound suppliers.

mutationSuite.method: Copied the freeze, the table, the checker and both bound suppliers into a scratchpad tree and ran the checker there, restoring a pristine copy between cases. No repository byte was modified; git reports zero modified tracked files at close.

cases.note: Caught at the digest gate rather than the selector gate, because renaming a key necessarily moves the bytes. Correct and stricter than v1's behaviour.

cases.mutation: modify S31-3's supplier, path and selector intact -- THE v1 BLOCKER
cases.note: v1 returned PASS at exit 0 on this exact mutation. S31-B1 repaired.
Proves digest-before-parse. S31-CX-B1 repaired: the failure is reported as DIGEST-MOVED, not as a JSON decode error.

cases.mutation: corrupt S31-3's supplier to non-JSON AND re-pin its digest to the corrupt bytes
cases.result: FAIL - S31-3: bound supplier is not JSON
cases.note: Confirms the parse path is still live and reachable once the digest gate passes, so the ordering fix did not turn the parse check into dead code.

cases.mutation: remove sha256 from a BOUND supplier in the table
cases.result: FAIL - S31-1: BOUND supplier has no sha256
cases.note: The repair is defended against its own erosion: a future edit that drops the digest field fails closed rather than silently reverting to v1 behaviour.

cases.result: FAIL - S31-3: textVerbatim does not match freeze item 3
cases.note: Per-item verbatim binding to the freeze, not just a count.

cases.mutation: append a line to the freeze file
cases.result: FAIL - ENVIRONMENT: freeze digest moved e809d439… -> 90dfb420…
FAIL - count drift: bound=2 unbound=6 expected {items:8, bound:3, unbound:6}

mutationSuite.readThisWay: Twelve cases, twelve correct outcomes. The mechanism is sound and materially stronger than v1's: v1 had four failure conditions of which one was advertised and unimplemented, and v2 has the same four all implemented plus five structural checks v1 did not have. My blocker is not against the mechanism. It is against what one of the two bound rows asserts, which no checker in this design can catch, because the checker verifies that a selector resolves and not that what it resolves to answers the item.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: In my v1 review I wrote under whatIDidNotCheck: 'The substantive adequacy of the two BOUND heads. I confirmed both selectors resolve and that each carries a whyThisHead rationale; I did not judge whether $.proofObligationsByClaimShape genuinely discharges freeze §3.1 item 1, or $.theSubstantiveDeltaIsPRESERVED item 3.' Codex's S31-CX-B2 was exactly that check on item 3, and it was a blocker. I disclosed the limit in advance, which is worth something, but disclosing a gap is not covering it, and the gap was where a blocker was sitting.
reviewerSelfCorrection.pattern: Verifying that a binding is well-formed rather than that it is true. In v1 I proved both selectors resolve and proved by mutation that the checker catches a missing one. Neither fact bears on whether the resolved head answers the freeze item, which is the only question the instrument ultimately exists to answer.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: I ran that check on both bound heads this time rather than only on the one Codex flagged. S31-3's rebinding is exact. S31-1's is not, and that is S31V2-01. Checking only the item another reviewer pointed at would have reproduced the same error one item over.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: I very nearly filed a second blocker asserting that whyThisHead's 'Later evaluation-proof versions drop the six claim shapes' is false. I had listed the corpus with ls piped to tail, which sorts lexicographically, so the listing ended at v9 and hid v10 through v13. On that truncated view v9 was the only later version, and since v9 carries the six shapes with identical content, the claim looked plainly false.
reviewerSelfCorrection.pattern: Same class as the whitespace-normalization misses I recorded earlier in this protocol: trusting a tool's default presentation of the corpus instead of enumerating it. A lexicographic sort over version-numbered files is a known trap and I walked into it.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: I re-swept all thirteen versions with a numeric sort before writing. v1 through v9 carry six shapes; v10 through v13 have the key ABSENT. The claim is TRUE and no blocker exists there. What survives is the much narrower S31V2-02, which is a SHOULD-FIX about v9 specifically. Recorded here rather than silently dropped, because the near-miss is the finding: had I filed it, I would have manufactured a blocker against a true statement.

whatIVerified: Subject digests at start and end: table 553b740a556a570bb5aa08b309c0cce1fec6a02375c18009ad5baf74a97d6bfd, checker c8f6dc6d7a9a67697246c49f77996175417ce1a7b2511de9edd929d62dfa20af, both unchanged and both matching the dispatch's recitals.

S31-B1 REPAIRED, verified by execution. Both BOUND suppliers now carry sha256 (key sets are path, selector, sha256, whyThisHead). The checker computes the live digest at line 122 and emits DIGEST-MOVED at 124. Mutation M-D -- the precise case that returned PASS at exit 0 under v1 -- now returns FAIL at exit 1. The authorityClaim/failsWhen contradiction is also gone: authorityClaim now recites three conditions (missing file, selector disappears, digest moves) that match failsWhen[0..2], with the freeze condition carried in remeasurementClause.

S31-CX-B1 REPAIRED, verified twice over. By construction: sha256 at line 122, DIGEST-MOVED with continue at 124-127, json.loads at 129 -- the digest gate strictly precedes the parse. By execution: M-E corrupts a supplier to non-JSON and the checker reports DIGEST-MOVED, not a decode error. M-F confirms the parse path is still reachable when the digest matches, so the fix did not create dead code.

S31-CX-B2 REPAIRED, and the repair is exact rather than merely different. Freeze item 3 is 'selected default custody/retention behavior, including whether any retention is implicit' -- two limbs. The new head, product-dispositions.v1.json#$.decisions.CD-RT-5.defaultPosture, carries durableDefault DURABLE_RETAINED for the first limb and implicitDurableRetention YES for the second, the latter mapping to the freeze wording almost word for word. whyThisHead is honest about the predecessor's error: v1's head 'only asserts delta-equivalence and does not contain those values', which is true.

S31-CX-A1 REPAIRED. The checker now enforces a 1:1 item mapping structurally: ids must equal S31-1..S31-N, item numbers must equal 1..N, duplicate ids are rejected, the row count must equal counts.items, and each row's textVerbatim must match the freeze item at the same index. M-H and M-I exercise two of these and both fail closed.

Every pinned digest reproduces against live bytes: S31-1's supplier at 4bb33f772c8c…, S31-3's at bbe24527f732…, the freeze at e809d4395f39…, and itemsVerbatim has exactly 8 entries. Baseline PASS bound=2 unbound=6 at exit 0.

The predecessor accounting is accurate and independently checkable on my half. predecessorSha256 is 2ceb0365… which is v1's digest as I measured it. My v1 verdict is pinned at c7abb1c43fcfe87cd274bdffa3fa6ffcf305f63ffc50ca1f1b587a9e7749d4af, matching my file exactly, and characterized as REJECT, which is what I returned. The Codex v1 verdict is pinned at b364bec3a2fea37430b3b01c5195a44f8b61bc1e74683391b9dc72096b90ea94 -- the same digest I recorded when I hashed it during the v1 review, so the pin is stable across dispatches.

No silent SATISFIED. whatThisDoesNotDo carries 'Does not mark DR-004 or DR-002 SATISFIED', and the header fields are status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, isThePhase1AInsertion false, documentClass BINDING-INSTRUMENT-CANDIDATE, lane R, registerRows DR-004 and DR-002.

The counts are internally consistent and externally confirmed: counts {items 8, bound 2, unbound 6} matches the items array, the checker independently reports bound=2 unbound=6, and M-K shows a falsified count is caught rather than trusted.
theErrorThisExistsToPrevent still states the v24-to-v28 partB_purgeSemantics case correctly, and 'Does not restore partB_purgeSemantics' survives in the refusal list.

The six UNBOUND items each carry a reason rather than a bare state, and S31-2's reason articulates the discipline this artifact holds itself to: 'Binding a class document as if it were a recipe would pretend the recipes are settled.' I used that sentence as the standard against which I judged S31-1.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of v2. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time. The Codex review of v1 I also did not read -- I know S31-CX-B1, S31-CX-B2 and S31-CX-A1 only through this artifact's own predecessorVerdictFindings and the dispatch, and I verified the repairs against the freeze and the suppliers rather than against Codex's statements of the defects. If those findings are mischaracterized in predecessorVerdictFindings, my verification would not detect it.

Whether any of the six UNBOUND items could now be bound. I verified the reasons are stated; I did not sweep the corpus for candidate suppliers for items 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. Under-binding reports less coverage than may exist, which is the safe direction, but it is unmeasured.

Whether product-dispositions.v1.json's CD-RT-5 is itself sound. I verified it answers freeze item 3's two limbs. I did not review the disposition's merits, and I note without judging it that CD-RT-5 records an override of a standing architectural recommendation and states its own consequence as 'The tool writes analysis evidence into a user's project before that user has been asked.' Whether that disposition should stand is not this instrument's question and is not mine here.

The checker's resolve() on selector forms the corpus does not exercise -- array indices, wildcards, or escaped dots in key names. S31-3's selector is the first multi-segment one in use ($.decisions.CD-RT-5.defaultPosture) and it works; deeper and non-dict forms remain untested.
Whether DR-004 and DR-002's owners will accept this instrument. It binds nothing and recommends nothing about their rows.

environment.note: Both subjects are untracked working-tree files at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the candidate is pre-adoption and binds NOTHING.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256; python3 for digest verification, shape comparison and a numerically-sorted sweep of all thirteen evaluation-proof versions; twelve-case executable mutation suite against a scratchpad copy with a pristine restore between cases

verdictNote: REJECT on one blocker, against a generation that is genuinely much better than its predecessor. All three named blockers landed, the checker gained five structural checks it did not have, and every one of twelve mutations fails closed. I am rejecting on the one thing no checker in this design can see: whether a bound head answers the freeze item it is bound to. That question defeated v1 at S31-3, was repaired there, and survives unexamined at S31-1 -- because in v1 I declined to ask it and this time Codex's finding pointed only at the item Codex had checked. The repair is likely small. The reason for the severity is that a coverage instrument whose count includes a partially-covered row misreports the one number it exists to produce.
